source.close_reason: Tuned git-cliff: added per-commit date-time (commit.author.timestamp) to changelog body template; commit bodies already rendered. Regenerated CHANGELOG [Unreleased] non-destructively (header preserved, additions only). No scope parsers added — fallthrough entries are merge/unconventional historical commits, not a scope taxonomy. Committed bc6cd42.
source.description:
git-cliff was rolled out across all ~/dev and ~/projects repos in one batch (362f104). This bead is the ack + tuning gate for THIS repo.

## WHAT LANDED
- changelog/cliff.toml — GENERIC type-based parsers only (feat->Added, fix->Fixed,
  perf->Performance, docs|chore|build|ci|test|refactor|style->Project maintenance,
  everything else->Other changes). Version-bump commits are skipped.
- header = "" on purpose, so the CHANGELOG keeps its own title and --prepend never
  stacks a second header on top of it.
- Commit links point at this repo's own origin remote.
- CHANGELOG.md: generated fresh if absent; otherwise --prepend --unreleased only.
  Verified non-destructive — 0 existing lines lost in every repo that had one.

## WHY THIS BEAD IS P0
The config is deliberately generic and is NOT tuned to this repo. Until someone acks it:
- Real work may be landing under 'Other changes' instead of a meaningful section.
- Scope names used by this repo's commits have no parser entry.

## TO DO
1. Run: git-cliff --config changelog/cliff.toml --unreleased  (inspect, do not write)
2. Count entries falling into 'Other changes'. If more than a couple, add scope parsers
   ABOVE the generic ones, e.g. { message = "^feat\\(api\\)", group = "API" }.
3. Document the scope taxonomy in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md so the agents that write the
   commits actually follow it — the taxonomy is useless if only the parser knows it.
4. If this repo had a hand-written CHANGELOG, reconcile the generated format against
   the existing style (they will not match).
5. Regenerate with --prepend --unreleased. NEVER use -o / plain generate on a repo with
   a hand-written CHANGELOG — it rebuilds from the git log and drops every hand-written
   line (measured: 362 lines would be lost in specialists).

## DO NOT
- Do not run git-cliff without --prepend on a repo that already has a CHANGELOG.
- Nothing was pushed. Review the commit before pushing.
source.notes:
RESWEEPED — config now renders commit BODIES, not just subjects.

The first sweep only templated {{ commit.message }}, throwing away the rich bodies the
agents already write. cliff.toml now renders {% if commit.body %}, so a changelog entry
carries the full rationale, bead id, PR number, and file/env details straight from git.
Verified on market-data: generated entries now match the hand-written ones in substance.

All changelogs were restored to their exact pre-sweep state and re-prepended.
Measured: 0 pre-existing lines lost in every repo that already had a CHANGELOG.

## REMAINING TUNING (this bead)
1. SCOPES — parsers are still generic (type-based only). Run:
     git-cliff --config changelog/cliff.toml --unreleased
   Count entries under 'Other changes'. Add repo-specific scope parsers ABOVE the
   generic ones, e.g. { message = "^feat\\(api\\)", group = "API" }.
2. COMMIT BODIES ARE NOW THE CHANGELOG. Document that in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md: the
   body is what readers see, so agents should write it for a reader, not a reviewer.
   Squash-merge commits currently dump the raw PR bullet list verbatim — verbose.
3. FORMAT — repos with a hand-written CHANGELOG have two styles stacked. Reconcile.

## HARD RULE
NEVER run git-cliff without --prepend on a repo that has a hand-written CHANGELOG.
It rebuilds from the git log and drops every hand-written line (measured: 362 lines
would be lost in specialists). Always: --unreleased --prepend.

Nothing was pushed. Review before pushing.
